ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two similar triangles in the figure. The triangle on the left is RST, the base RT is labeled 15, the hypotenuse RS is labeled 20.7, and side ST is labeled 10; angle R is 27°, angle T is 110°, and angle S is 43°. The triangle on the right is EFG, the base EF is labeled 11.25; angle E is 27°, angle F is 110°, so the corresponding angle G is 43°. The problem asks to find EG. Reasoning: From the angle correspondence relationship, it can be known that R ↔ E, T ↔ F, S ↔ G, so side RT corresponds to EF, and side RS corresponds to EG. The similarity ratio from the left triangle to the right triangle is EF/RT = 11.25/15 = 0.75. Therefore EG = RS × 0.75 = 20.7 × 0.75 = 15.525.
